structural.why: changes geometry or whether a state is reachable, so a plausible value would be worse than none

declared-alternative.why: a contract field would answer it outright, so the fix is that field plus the prompt requirement, not a smarter heuristic

unknown-severity.why: changes what a glyph or role looks like rather than where it sits: emit the node, name the unknown, never pick a variant silently

decorative.why: changes paint only, no target can express it, and the comment is the honest record that the design asked

ignored-or-gate.why: cannot be read as a value at all (a keyframe, an interaction): report it, emit nothing, never translate a duration into a motion the framework lacks

unmapped-longhand.why: capture always produces it and this source never declares it: named so a future export cannot slip through, worth nothing today

properties.note: One @keyframes (mj-rise) plus a single animation: on a Home panel; a second @keyframes (mj-spin) is declared and never used. Nothing here gates a state a target has to reach.
properties.fix: Nothing to emit: there is no entrance motion for a target to reproduce. If a motion is ever meant to be real, declare it as a state (data-state) or a manifest motion token; a CSS animation is readable as neither.

properties.note: expands to background-color, background-image and the rest of the layer list, and it DOES reset them (measured). All 44 values in this export are a role color, transparent, or a hole: 0 url() and 0 gradient anywhere in a background value (measured), so no image layer reaches the IR.
it would need a gradient or a url, and this export has neither (measured: 0 url() and 0 gradient in any background value)
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: expands to border-width, border-style, border-color, and it DOES reset those three (measured) but NOT border-radius (measured) -- which is why the 28 rounded corners in this export survive a bare `border:`.

One overlay offset, bottom:var(--md-sys-space-8) on the PodcastCard cover badge -- the badge spec/01 names as the case that maps honestly to Box plus offset. The distance is right; the subject is undeclared.
properties.fix: Same as left: name the overlaid box and this becomes a Box alignment plus offset rather than a coordinate.

properties.note: Seven boxes, six of them component roots: the EpisodeRow, NowPlayingBar and PodcastCard roots at width:100%, a Home frame wrapper at width:{{w}}, Home's absolute badge and its 32px button; the seventh is the board root at min-height:100vh. Compose and React Native have no box-sizing at all, so whether padding grows those roots or eats into them is exactly the border-and-padding trap spec/04 warns about, and the export answers it for these seven only.
properties.fix: Add a box-sizing field to the manifest, or state in the prompt that every box measures content-box so the emitter subtracts padding and border the way CSS did. Either answer works; the current silence is what makes it a guess.

properties.note: The text-cursor tint on the Home search input (1x, --md-sys-color-primary). Nothing about layout depends on it.
properties.fix: No contract change: the target takes the caret from its theme (Compose cursorBrush, RN selectionColor). If it should track a role, put data-token on that input instead of a caret-color.

properties.note: expands to flex-grow, flex-shrink, flex-basis and DOES reset them (measured). spec/04 maps `flex: 1` and `flex: 0 0 auto` as whole values, so the longhands are the honest seam for anything else.

spec/04 maps `flex: 1` and `flex: 0 0 auto` as whole values, so the flex-shrink longhand on its own is named nowhere. It matters the moment an export writes the longhand directly, because shrinking is what decides whether a label truncates or wraps.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: expands to font-style, font-variant, font-weight, font-stretch, font-size, line-height, font-family, and DOES reset them (measured) -- but NOT letter-spacing (measured), which is why the 23 separate letter-spacing declarations in this export are real intent and not leftovers the font shorthand would have eaten. Every one of the 65 values is a single var(--md-sys-typescale-<role>) across 10 roles, with 0 literal sizes (measured).

Named by no spec row. This export never sets it, so capture always reads the default 100%; it is recorded because it is one of the seven longhands the font shorthand resets, so a future `font: condensed ...` would arrive owned by nothing.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: Named by no spec row. Italic never appears in this export, so there is no case to map yet; it is listed because capture reads it on every element and a design that does use italic today would emit silently wrong.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: Named by no spec row. Do not confuse it with font-variation-settings, which this export does use and which is a separate gap: font-variant is the older capabilities shorthand and font-variation-settings is the variable-font axis list.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: tabular-nums on the two elapsed/duration readouts (NowPlayingBar, EpisodeRow). Those digits need fixed widths or the running time jitters, and no computed font tells a target that.
properties.fix: Declare it: a data-numeric="tabular" attribute, or a typography role in tokens.json carrying a tabular flag. That is what becomes FontFeature "tnum" in Compose and fontVariant: ["tabular-nums"] in RN.

properties.note: 'FILL' 1 on 5 Material Symbols spans plus one hole ({{ subFill }}). This is the icon font's fill axis: it decides whether the glyph is outlined or filled, so it changes which icon the design chose, not just how it was drawn.
properties.fix: Declare the glyph and its fill as intent: data-icon="volume_up" plus a filled/outlined flag. Then the converter names the right asset in the target icon set instead of picking between two variants the font can draw.

properties.note: One real track list (repeat(auto-fill, minmax(400px, 1fr))) on a board frame grid plus one hole ({{ gridCols }}) on the Home grid. The computed value resolves to N fixed tracks, which is a reading of the viewport, not the design decision.
properties.fix: Carry data-grid-min="140" on the grid container, which spec/01 already requires. minmax(400px, 1fr) is exactly what Adaptive() needs, and it is the one value a computed grid-template-columns cannot be reversed into.

properties.note: Two overlay offsets: position:absolute; left:26px; top:6px on a Home badge, and left:var(--md-sys-space-8) with bottom on the PodcastCard cover badge. Neither names the box it overlays, which is exactly what spec/01 says an absolute must declare.
properties.fix: Name the overlaid box. spec/01 already allows an absolute as a declared overlay that maps to Box plus offset; a data-overlay (or data-box on the parent) turns these two coordinates into a component instead of a screenshot.

properties.note: expands to the four margin-* longhands and DOES reset them (measured), so order inside one style attribute decides the result. spec/03 resolves spacing from the longhands, which is the right seam.

Six ceilings, and only one is the design. Read element by element: max-width:720px caps the Home search row (a real component constraint), while 1400px is the board header, 1320px (twice) are board frame grids whose own text reads "NowPlayingBar full width at every window size" and "Playing, 40% - expanded and medium", and 760px/560px cap board prose. Five of six are presentation chrome a capture reads as component geometry, and nothing in the source tells them apart.
properties.fix: Two cheap ways out: give the board its own stylesheet a capture can exclude, or let the manifest say which frames are board scaffolding rather than screens. Until one exists the class has to be structural and stop on all six: emitting 1320.dp as a component width is worse than refusing.

properties.note: Six declarations, and the token expands to outline-color/style/width (measured) which no spec owns either, so nothing dissolves here. Three are outline: none on focusable elements (button, input, span), an accessibility decision because it removes the default focus ring; three are a hole ({{ cardOutline }}, {{ btnOutline }}, {{ searchOutline }}) that paints a selected or focused ring from a prop.
properties.fix: For the outline: none rows, declare that focus is drawn some other way, or drop the reset and let the target draw its own state layer. For the holes, the prop already names the state: put that state in data-state and the target emits a focus/selected branch instead of a static ring.

properties.note: Named by no spec row. outline is itself an unmapped gap, so its three longhands inherit that: this row exists so translating outline later cannot quietly skip the color and default it to the text color.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: 2px on 3 elements, always beside an outline above. It moves the ring off the edge, so the ring is either decoration or an overlay box, and no target can tell which without being told.
properties.fix: Same decision as outline: an overlay ring is a declared overlay (Box plus offset in Compose), focus feedback is a state. Do not emit an offset belonging to neither.

properties.note: Named by no spec row. In this export it is only ever `none` or the value a hole supplies; it decides whether a focus ring exists at all, which is an accessibility answer rather than a style, and it belongs with the outline gap above.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: Named by no spec row. Measured: the outline shorthand DOES reset it, so a bare `outline: none` silently changes it too, and a ring width is the number a target would need to draw the ring at all.
properties.fix: Add the mapping row before a target ever has to read it. Nothing emits from it today, so no value is lost and nothing is invented.

properties.note: expands to overflow-x and overflow-y and DOES reset them (measured). spec/03 detects a scroll container by reading overflow-y, so the longhand is where that decision has to live -- and a naive value reader that stops at a {{ }} hole loses all 3 of them.
expands to the four padding-* longhands and DOES reset them (measured).

Thin owner on purpose: the one spec row for this property resolves `position: sticky`. What this export uses is relative (3x) and absolute (2x), and spec/01 covers those as a declared overlay with no attribute yet. Recorded so the thinness is visible instead of looking settled.
The scrollbar thumb and trough tint on 3 Home scroll panes, from --md-sys-color-outline-variant and --md-sys-color-surface.
properties.fix: No action: Compose and RN draw their own scrollbars and the target theme decides. A comment naming the design tint is honest; inventing a Scrollbar composable is not.

properties.note: scrollbar-width: thin on the same 3 Home panes. It is also evidence the pane scrolls, which the capture already reads from overflow.
properties.fix: No action: a platform scrollbar decision, reported as info. Nothing is lost by not translating it.

properties.note: text-wrap: pretty on 5 paragraphs (board captions, Home and PodcastCard copy). It changes where lines break, which is a rendering nicety no target exposes as a property.
properties.fix: Nothing to declare: line breaking is the target text engine's job. Worth one comment on the emitted text node so a human knows the design cared about ragging.

properties.note: One overlay offset, top:6px on the Home badge, paired with the left above. An offset with no named subject.
properties.fix: Same as left: declare what the badge overlays and top becomes an offset inside that Box.

properties.note: All 3 occurrences are inside the two @keyframes blocks (rotate(360deg) in mj-spin, translateY(100%)/translateY(0) in mj-rise). None is a transform: in component markup, so the export does not use transform for spacing, which is the thing spec/01 forbids.
properties.fix: Nothing to emit: corner-cases already says never turn a duration into a motion the framework does not have, and the same holds for the transform a keyframe animates. A permanent offset belongs in padding, an offset, or a declared overlay, not in the end state of an animation.

properties.note: expands to white-space-collapse and text-wrap-mode, and the capture reads both; spec/04 and spec/05 map the shorthand value (nowrap), so the longhands are named for completeness.
